chunks: And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who visited the House, performed Tawaf around the House, and between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, then returned. An eye (evil eye/weakness) overcame him on the road, and he slept until morning. He said: 'Upon him is a sheep.'

This does not contradict what the first report contained from his statement, except if you have left Mecca, because that report is applied to one who left Mecca and passed the pass of the Madinians, for it is permissible for him to sleep while in the state we described.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the hills for Sa'i)
key_terms.عَقَبَةَ الْمَدَنِيِّينَ: The pass of the Madinians (a specific location on the road from Mecca)
key_terms.عَيْنُهُ: His eye (referring to evil eye or physical weakness)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a pilgrim who falls ill or is overcome by weakness during the return journey from Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling of *Qada' al-Hajj* for a pilgrim who, after completing the core rites, fell ill or was overcome by the evil eye during the return journey. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes offering a sheep as compensation, specifying that this ruling applies to those who had already departed Mecca and passed the boundary of the Madain, distinguishing it from those still within the sacred precincts.
